claim: Layang-Layang, Sabah Trough and Kinabalu Basin are three structural positions within one collision system (lower plate / foredeep / upper plate), not three independent basins.

One collision (COLLISION_MM), three opposite expressions: RU drowning without major erosion on the lower plate; foredeep onset in the trough; DRU uplift-erosion on the upper plate. They are physically different surfaces with different seismic signatures.
source: Arif ENTERPRISE relay + Clift et al. 2008 + Hinz 1985
confidence: MED-HIGH for order, LOW for exact age

claim: Rifted Dangerous Grounds crust continues SE beneath Neogene Borneo sediments at least halfway between the Sabah shelf and slope toe; part of Kinabalu is stacked above Layang-Layang crust at depth.
source: Arif ENTERPRISE relay 2026-09-30 (INTERPRET — untested by cross-trough dip line)

claim: SCS seafloor spreading terminated after ~16 Ma when the Dangerous Grounds collided with and jammed the Borneo trench; spreading onset ~33-32 Ma (C12) per IODP Exp 349.
source: Clift et al. 2008; IODP Expedition 349 results (public)

claim: Subduction polarity and timing beneath NW Borneo is unresolved: older SE-directed proto-SCS subduction vs newer continental underthrusting from ~base Miocene. HOLD; both recorded; do not average.
source: Arif ENTERPRISE relay 2026-09-30 + public literature debate

claim: BANGKIT (PROPOSED, not adopted): a Late Miocene lithospheric-rebalancing event beneath Sabah drives post-16 Ma deformation independent of renewed plate collision. Evidence verified 2026-09-30: uplift/exhumation ~8–3 Ma at >7 mm/yr (Menier et al. 2017); Late-Miocene apatite+zircon cooling of the Crocker belt (JGS 2000 thermochronology); PSCS slab remnant beneath Sabah confirmed geophysically (Cornwell et al. 2025 JGR W-dipping discontinuity 45–55 km; Pilia et al. 2023; Yu et al. 2021; Shi et al. 2020). Mechanism OPEN (break-off vs delamination vs dripping vs crustal melting). Kinabalu granite INTRUSION age UNVERIFIED (K-Ar range to 14 Ma contested); an enterprise-AI-analysis 9–7 Ma window is narrower than the evidence. SRU (9–8.5 Ma) sits at the onset edge — BANGKIT as SRU driver plausible, unproven.
source: Enterprise AI analysis 2026-09-30 (names INVENTED, pending F13; tool de-referenced 2026-10-08) + FI-003 source verification 2026-09-30 (search-snippet class; full texts not yet read)

claim: GEMPA (PROPOSED, not adopted): present-day deformation of Sabah is real and mixed-regime — 2015 Ranau Mw 6.0; GPS NW motion of coastal Sabah; uplift-driven gravitational collapse with extensional accommodation; GNSS at Ranau records BOTH NW-SE compression and extension. Do not label extension-only or compression-only.
source: FI-003 source verification 2026-09-30 (GSM papers, GPS literature — snippet class)

claim: Invariance across Layang-Layang, Sabah Trough and Kinabalu is TOPOLOGICAL, not chronological: no single unconformity reflector runs through all three provinces. What persists where preserved is the ORDER of events (RETAK -> BEBAS -> LANGGAR -> SABAR -> SENJA) and the ARRANGEMENT of surfaces around the collision; reflectors and absolute ages do not persist. LANGGAR (AM-07) is the one surface family recorded on BOTH plates - as RU (drowning, lower plate), base of foredeep fill (trough), DRU (uplift+erosion, upper plate) - in three different windows. SABAR (UIU) and SENJA (SRU) are upper-plate only.
source: Arif (F13 SOVEREIGN) settlement 2026-10-01; Levell (1987) unconformity->onlap->correlative conformity; literature-consistent
falsifier: A reflector traced continuously through all three provinces with one event identity for any single unconformity; or a province where the preserved event order differs from the ladder.

claim: Geometric rule (two surface families): surfaces OLDER than LANGGAR belong to the lower plate - formed on Dangerous Grounds crust, present everywhere, dipping SE beneath the Kinabalu wedge, imaged only on the NW side. Surfaces YOUNGER than LANGGAR belong to the upper plate - unconformities in Kinabalu fading NW-ward into the trough. The Sabah Trough is a STRATIGRAPHIC SUTURE where the two families meet: surfaces are hard to trace there because two clocks overlap. The ~3 Myr separation RU (16.9-15.5) -> foredeep onset (16-15) -> DRU (13.5-12.5) is the time the collision load took to move from lower to upper plate; one label would hide the mechanism.
falsifier: A post-LANGGAR erosive unconformity confirmed on the lower plate (Layang/DG side), or a pre-LANGGAR surface imaged continuously inside the Kinabalu wedge above the detachment - either breaks the family partition.
